cases.name: both-branches-fire-then-merge-then-one-more
cases.note: AND-split fans StartEvent.main[0] out to HelloAction + HelloAction 1 (parallel). Each hits GET /foobar. The AND-join Merge (n8n mode: chooseBranch, chooseBranchMode: waitForAll, output: empty) synchronizes on both branches and emits ONE downstream execution. HelloAction 2 sits after the merge and must fire EXACTLY ONCE — proving the join emits a single token, not one per input branch. Total WireMock journal: 3 GET /foobar requests (2 pre-merge + 1 post-merge). If the merge mode were 'append' the journal would show 4 (post-merge fires twice); if it were 'combine/combineAll' it would show 4 (2x2 cross product = 2 downstream runs).
